name: Designating and Managing a Conservation Area
fact: Historic England explains conservation areas are designated by local planning authorities to preserve or enhance special architectural or historic character and should be supported by appraisal and management-plan evidence.
gate: Conservation-area overlap is not automatic refusal or approval; exact local appraisal, management plan, Article 4 controls and proposal effect must be checked.

name: Historic Environment Records
fact: Historic England's HER guidance, updated 23 March 2026, describes local Historic Environment Records as dynamic primary sources for archaeology, built heritage, planning and development-control work.
gate: A HER hit is an information starting point, not an archaeological field evaluation, definitive absence test or development consent.

name: Greater London Archaeological Priority Areas
fact: Historic England explains Greater London Archaeological Priority Areas use evidence from the GLHER and tiered risk to highlight archaeological sensitivity to development.
gate: APA tier is a screening/risk model, not proof archaeology exists at a parcel or that evaluation/mitigation is unnecessary outside an APA.

name: Greater London Historic Environment Record
fact: Historic England's GLHER provides development-related historic-environment searches and from 1 April 2026 uses a revised search pricing/service structure.
gate: Ordering or receiving a GLHER search is not archaeological evaluation or planning approval; exact event/source records and site conditions still matter.

name: Managing archaeological projects in Greater London
fact: Historic England states its current Greater London archaeological standards/guidance version is dated February 2026 and sets project expectations by site type.
gate: Standards define how investigation should be undertaken; they do not prove a site has been investigated or that archaeological risk is resolved.

name: Historic England archaeology technical advice
fact: Historic England's archaeology advice brings together technical, policy and management guidance including survey, archaeological science, recording and planning-related guidance.
gate: Guidance availability is not site evidence; exact desk-based assessment, field evaluation and HER data remain required where relevant.

name: Historic England latest advice and guidance
fact: Historic England's latest-guidance page, updated 30 June 2026, identifies newly published and revised heritage advice and technical guidance.
gate: Use the latest applicable guidance version but do not treat guidance publication as a site-specific statutory decision.

name: Planning Data listed building dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 382,250 listed-building records collected through 21 July 2026 and explicitly states the dataset shows a point within the listed building and does not define the affected listing extent.
gate: Never use listed-building point data as legal boundary/curtilage; verify the NHLE official entry and exact legal scope.

name: Planning Data listed building outline dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 121,057 listed-building outlines but states coverage is incomplete, MHCLG-created and does not consistently show listed-building curtilage for planning purposes.
gate: Outline geometry is indicative only and must not be treated as definitive curtilage or legal extent.

name: Planning Data listed building grade
fact: Planning Data publishes the authoritative listed-building grade taxonomy I, II* and II.
gate: Grade indicates national significance category but does not determine proposal harm, consent outcome or exact extent.

name: Planning Data scheduled monument dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 20,150 scheduled-monument records with collector/new-data dates of 22 July 2026 and notes some MHCLG-created data pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Use the current Historic England NHLE legal entry/geometry for exact scheduled extent; platform aggregation alone is not sufficient for consent decisions.

name: Planning Data conservation area dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 11,050 conservation-area records from 158 providers through 22 July 2026 but explicitly describes the dataset as incomplete and containing duplicates/mixed provenance.
gate: No platform hit is not proof of no conservation area, and duplicate/secondary geometry must be reconciled with the current LPA designation.

name: Planning Data conservation area document dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 13,874 conservation-area documents from 86 providers with collection through 21 July 2026 and mixed provenance.
gate: Document index presence does not establish which appraisal/management plan is current or legally operative; verify the LPA source and dates.

name: Planning Data conservation area document types
fact: Planning Data defines six conservation-area document types including appraisal, notice, designation report, area map, management plan and design guidance.
gate: Document type classification is schema metadata, not evidence that a current document exists for a specific conservation area.

name: Planning Data historic parks and gardens
fact: Planning Data reports 1,723 historic parks and gardens with collection through 20 July 2026 and newest data found 18 July 2026.
gate: Dataset intersection identifies a designated landscape context but is not a separate consent or impact conclusion.

name: Planning Data park and garden grade
fact: Planning Data defines registered park-and-garden grades I, II* and II.
gate: Grade is significance classification only; exact proposal effects, setting and planning balance remain required.

name: Planning Data battlefield dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 94 battlefield records from authoritative sources, but the newest data found date shown is 12 February 2025 despite a July 2026 collector run.
gate: Collector freshness is not underlying-data freshness; recheck Historic England NHLE before relying on the platform copy.

name: Planning Data World Heritage Site dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 40 World Heritage Site records with collection through 21 July 2026 and notes UNESCO holds the definitive World Heritage list while platform provenance is mixed.
gate: Planning Data geometry is screening/context; confirm UNESCO/Historic England management and exact planning controls before parcel conclusions.

name: Planning Data World Heritage Site buffer zones
fact: Planning Data reports 9 World Heritage Site buffer-zone records and mixed provenance, with newest data found 30 June 2026.
gate: Absence of a platform buffer-zone record does not prove no setting/buffer implications; verify the relevant WHS management plan and authoritative mapping.

name: Planning Data certificate of immunity dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 251 Certificates of Immunity with collection/new-data dates in June 2026 and mixed provenance sourced around Historic England data.
gate: COI effect is time-bounded and building-listing-specific; check the exact current certificate end date and other designations.

name: Planning Data building preservation notice dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 9 Building Preservation Notices and states the dataset is MHCLG-created pending authoritative LPA publication/specification.
gate: Treat as discovery only; verify the live BPN directly with the LPA/Historic England because BPN protection is temporary and the national dataset is limited.

name: Heritage at Risk selection criteria
fact: Historic England explains Heritage at Risk inclusion requires both an eligible designation category and an assessment that the asset is at risk, with category-specific methodologies.
gate: Heritage-at-risk status is condition/vulnerability evidence, not planning permission, viability or automatic development opportunity.

name: Heritage at Risk latest findings 2025
fact: Historic England's latest findings report 4,891 entries on the 2025 Heritage at Risk Register, published 6 November 2025, with annual additions and removals.
gate: HAR is an annual snapshot and must not be treated as live condition after material change without current local/site evidence.

name: Heritage at Risk register search
fact: Historic England's current Heritage at Risk search separates categories and risk fields such as condition, vulnerability and trend across listed buildings, scheduled monuments, conservation areas and other assets.
gate: Risk category/trend describes heritage condition and vulnerability; it does not determine planning outcome or confirm acquisition/development feasibility.
